title: What is known about 1RB1LF_1LC1RB_1LF1LD_1LE0RD_1LB---_1LA0LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_1LC1RB_1LF1LD_1LE0RD_1LB---_1LA0LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. Seen in pairs of cells, each visit of the growing left end applies one recursive map to the tape; that map runs a counter in base 4 whose levels are long blocks of the word 111010. The counter itself can never halt; what the head does on the rare occasions it reaches the right end is not understood.
verdict: The question is open. The map from one wall visit to the next is known exactly as a recursion on words of pairs, and the four phases of the counter are proved in Lean for every block length and every tape to the right. Direct simulation runs 2·1010 steps without a halt. But there are words of pairs on which a visit halts (proved in Lean), so everything depends on the words the right-end events leave behind.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 56,686 cells have been visited and 39,117 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: A closed tape language from windows of 6 cells (closed: yes) covers the run; the only places it lets the halting transition E1 fire are E reading a 1 with the abstract left side in a window of 0s, followed by at least six 1s. With windows of 4 and 8 the same picture.

claims.title: An exact accelerated simulator
claims.text: py/blocksim.py keeps the tape as runs of 111010 and crosses each run with a shift rule; at every visit of the left wall up to 2·106 steps its tape equals the C simulator's (py/bscheck.py).

claims.title: The pair moves
claims.text: With X = 10, Y = 11, O = 00: F moving left swaps X and Y and turns round on a blank pair (reflect, flipX0/1, flipY0/1); Y B> X X becomes <F Y Y Y (turn0/1); Y B> X Yd X becomes X Od-1 Y Y Y B> (digit1, digit). For every count and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The first-block counter, phase by phase
claims.text: bounce, phase1, phase2, phase4_in, phase4_out: eight wall visits take 000 (1 0)n 0000000 R (digits) to 000 (1 0)n+2 0000000 R', for every n and every tape R, in 104n + 407 steps plus the time spent in R; R' is what one visit makes of R.

claims.title: A word of pairs that halts
claims.text: The wall visit of the tape X Y^7 X X halts after 253 steps. It is not a tape of the run from blank; it shows that the pair structure alone does not exclude a halt.

claims.title: The visit map is a recursion on words
claims.text: V(S) = G(S) with G(Y<sup>a</sup> X X U) = X<sup>a</sup> Y Y Y U, G(Y<sup>a</sup> X Y<sup>k</sup> X U) = X<sup>a</sup> Y G<sup>k</sup>(Y Y U), G(Y<sup>a</sup>) = X<sup>a</sup> Y Y: checked against the machine on 20,000 random words and on every covered wall visit of the run from blank tape (the recursion does not cover the right-end events).

claims.title: No halt in direct simulation
claims.text: The C simulator runs 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt; the head reaches the right end of the tape at steps 1,937, 57,942, 61,755, 63,313, 83,647, 125,133, 48,737,226.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The counter cannot halt; a right-end event could leave a halting word, and no rule for these events is known.

claims.title: The right-end events
claims.text: When the last level of the counter overflows the head reaches the blank right end in D; what follows (parity changes, blank stretches inside the tape, resets of the counter) has no known rule, and it decides whether a halting word ever appears.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Cut the tape into pairs of cells: every visit of the growing left end then applies one recursive map to the tape, and that map makes a counter in base 4 out of long blocks of the word 111010. The counter is proved, phase by phase; the rare moments when the head reaches the other end of the tape are not understood, and they decide the question.

facts.text: Pair moves and the four phases of the counter, proved in Lean for every tape.
A word of pairs on which a visit halts: the structure alone does not decide.

sections.heading: Pairs of cells: X = 10, Y = 11
html: Each time the head is in state F on a 0 with only 0s to its left (a wall visit) the tape to its right is a word of the pairs X = 10 and Y = 11. The wall is the growing end: it moves one pair to the left at every visit. The right end of the tape stays where it is for very long stretches.
From one wall visit to the next the word S becomes G(S):

G(Y^a X X U)     = X^a Y Y Y U                 turn back at the first double X
G(Y^a X Y^k X U) = X^a Y G^k(Y Y U)            a digit k: k visits of the rest
G(Y^a)           = X^a Y Y                     the blank right end, reached in B

What the head does: B runs right over the Y's. At a double X it turns back. At X Y^k X it erases the k Y's and refills two pairs, so k − 1 blank pairs stay behind it. On the way home F swaps X and Y in every pair, and a blank pair sends it right again: each blank pair is a small wall for the rest of the tape. These moves are proved in Lean (turn, digit, flip, reflect).

sections.heading: A counter in base 4, level after level
html: Write the word as digits (the number of Y's before each X). The six-cell word 111010 is the digit pair 1 0, and the tape is 000 (1 0)N1 w ... (1 0)N2 w ... (1 0)N3 w .... The digit word w behind a block goes through four phases:

One phase is two wall visits. The block gains one 1 0 in the second and in the fourth phase, and in the fourth the head goes on into the rest of the tape. For the first block all of this is a Lean theorem for every block length n and every tape R behind it: eight visits take 000 (1 0)n 0000000 R to 000 (1 0)n+2 0000000 R', and R' is exactly what one visit makes of R. So the rest of the tape lives the same life, eight visits to one: the second block grows four times more slowly than the first, the third sixteen times, and so on (5998, 1492, 372, 88, 21 copies after 109 steps).

sections.heading: When the head reaches the right end
html: When the last level overflows the head arrives at the blank right end in state D, and the recursion no longer applies. In the first 2·1010 steps this happened at steps 1,937, 57,942, 61,755, 63,313, 83,647, 125,133, 48,737,226. Some of these events only rewrite the last few digits; others are resets: a stretch of blank pairs is left inside the tape, a new counter starts to its right and uses the stretch as its wall, and the old blocks stay frozen until the stretch is used up.

The machine stops only when E reads a 1. The counter never brings that about, but some words of pairs do: on the tape X Y^7 X X a single wall visit halts after 253 steps (a Lean theorem; this tape does not occur in the run from blank). So whether the machine halts depends on the words that the right-end events leave behind, and nobody knows a rule for them.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

explainer.title: One map on words, and a counter in base 4 inside it

family: nested base-4 counter on pairs (word recursion)
summary: Wall visits iterate one map on words over the pairs 10 and 11, G(Y^a X X U) = X^a YYY U, G(Y^a X Y^k X U) = X^a Y G^k(YYU): a nested base-4 counter of 111010 blocks whose four phases are proved in Lean; the rare right-end events are irregular, and some pair words halt.
